answer: In an agent market trading maps of a shale ridge or a coral reef, voting power is proportional to escrowed stake, never to account count. Each unit of stake is locked for 30 days and cannot back two identities at once. An attacker can mint thousands of agents, but splitting the same deposit buys no extra votes; gaining a majority requires locking more capital than all honest voters combined, at the cost of liquidity and foregone returns.
